name: Hadlai
overview: Hadlai was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim, noted in Scripture as the father of Amasa. His primary biblical significance arises from his relationship to Amasa, who played a role in assisting the defeated Judaites. Beyond this, the biblical record provides limited detail about Hadlai himself.
namesAndTitles: The name Hadlai means 'resting; fat, stout' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name without indication of divine origin. This meaning may suggest characteristics of strength or stability, though Scripture does not elaborate further on the significance of his name.
familyAndRelationships: Hadlai is identified as the father of Amasa, who is noted for aiding the defeated Judaites. He is also explicitly recorded as a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim. Scripture does not provide additional family relationships beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Hadlai's importance in the biblical narrative is primarily through his son Amasa, who was involved in supporting the Judaites after their defeat. This connection situates Hadlai within the tribal framework of Ephraim and links him to a moment of intertribal assistance recorded in Scripture. While Hadlai himself is not the focus of detailed events, his familial link underscores the interconnectedness of Israel's tribes during times of conflict.
